DBSCAN builds clusters by expanding through regions where points are sufficiently
dense. Step through the algorithm on a noisy concentric-circle dataset.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The circle shows the current point's ε-neighborhood. If it contains at least
`min_samples` points **including the current point**, the point is a core point:
its neighbors can continue expanding the cluster. A non-core point cannot
expand a cluster; it may become a border point, or remain noise.
:::

The fixed dataset matches the accompanying notebook: `make_circles(n_samples=100,
factor=0.5, noise=0.05, random_state=170)`. DBSCAN uses the coordinates, not
the original ring labels. Changing a parameter restarts the algorithm.

    <label for="dbscan-min-samples"><span>Minimum points, <code>min_samples</code></span><input id="dbscan-min-samples" type="range" min="2" max="12" step="1" value="4"><output id="dbscan-min-value">4</output></label>
